description: Dispatch an async job that triggers (Request Campaign) a campaign for up to 100 leads, with optional campaign tokens, and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished success and request_id. Destructive-class write action: the campaign's flow runs against real people, is irreversible, and is visible outside this system (it may send email, alert sales, change scoring, or move program status). Marketo's REST API exposes no way to read a campaign's flow steps first and no dry-run, so a caller cannot establish what this will do before it happens — trigger only campaigns you authored.
embedding_description: Run a Marketo trigger campaign (Request Campaign API) against up to 100 leads by id — the verb that FIRES marketing automation at real people: email, sales alerts, scoring and program-status changes, irreversible and visible outside this system. Flow steps are readable only by a human in the Marketo UI; effects surface afterwards via get_activities. Trigger only campaigns you authored.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status) and status 'queued'. The completed job result is a dict with success (bool) and request_id.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: A queued job is not a triggered campaign: give the job_id and poll check_marketo_job_status. Once completed, confirm success and note the request_id; the actual marketing effects (emails sent, etc.) happen inside Marketo asynchronously. success only means Marketo accepted the request, never that the effects were the intended ones: the flow was not inspectable beforehand. To learn what actually happened, read the activity log with get_activities afterwards.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never say the campaign was triggered from THIS verb's response -- it carries only the job handle. Marketo's acceptance is reported only once check_marketo_job_status reports status=completed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate a campaign request and dispatch a background job that triggers the campaign for a batch of leads in the configured Marketo instance.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Refused at dispatch, before any vendor call and with no job created: marketo.invalid_params for missing campaign_id/lead_ids, more than 100 lead_ids, a malformed tokens entry, or missing session_id/flow_id in the calling context. Reported later in check_marketo_job_status's error field: marketo.object_not_found: the campaign_id doesn't exist. marketo.validation_failed: the campaign isn't a trigger campaign, or a token name doesn't match one defined on it. marketo.not_configured: no marketo_instance address-book entry. marketo.permission_denied: the API user's Role lacks Execute Campaign — this permission is NOT checked by check_setup (unverifiable without actually triggering a campaign), so this may be the FIRST signal of the gap. A transport fault after dispatch may follow a vendor mutation.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.object_not_found: confirm the campaign_id via list_campaigns. marketo.validation_failed: check the campaign type in Marketo and the token names against the campaign's defined tokens. marketo.permission_denied: add 'Execute Campaign' under Admin > Users & Roles > Roles > <the API role> > Access API, then retry. After a transport fault, check get_activities for the campaign request before triggering again: a second trigger runs the flow against the same people again.
